command: see run.sh: build novel GTF + minimal classification; adjudicate --bam <ONT bam>; scan_variant_axis.py over the novel junctions vs the HG001 haplotype; analyze.py
data_provenance: real public ENCODE GM12878 ONT direct-RNA (ENCFF440ZML, minimap2 -ax splice -uf); 285 caller-novel chains (IsoQuant+Bambu+ESPRESSO combine); reference-bias scan vs NA12878=HG001 GIAB v4.2.1 SNV-consensus haplotype. Public data only, no private data.
notes: Real-data robustness of the optional BAM mapping axis. (1) The terminal soft-clip fraction, never a default gate and removed in 0.0.8, fired on 134/191 (70%) of junctions on real ONT dRNA in the last run that measured it (adapter/poly-A read ends). (2) The HiFi-calibrated 0.5 gates are chemistry-dependent: ONT's intrinsic indel error makes indel_near fire on 128/190 (67%) and it does not separate single (0.63) from >=2-caller (0.667) chains; the older low_mapq/supplementary signals barely fire (9/190, 3/190). The mapping axis is opt-in (--bam) and its thresholds need re-calibration per chemistry. (3) The sequence-level consensus axis separates the same data independently of chemistry (254 single vs 31 reproducible). (4) Reference-bias rescue fires 0/1364: GM12878=NA12878 is GIAB reference-grade, so the base rate is ~0; the rescue's value lies with divergent / non-reference genomes (cf. giab_cohort_rescue: 137 across 4 personalized genomes). Small-N caveat on >=2-caller (31). (5) 0.0.7 whole-chain read support works on real ONT dRNA with exact coordinates: 94.5% of splice sites among near-matching reads are exact, 154/285 chains have >= 3 exact full-chain reads on the isoform's strand (chain_wobble.py counts 155 without the strand check; a +-5 bp tolerance would add about 20), 71% of >=2-caller chains vs 52% of single-caller ones; no tolerance is needed. With --platform ont the indel-near gate is off and these chains become NOVEL_PROBABLE (147) instead of being held UNCONFIRMED by the mapping sign (129 under the HiFi defaults; ARTIFACT before ruleset 0.0.5). No truth here: this is robustness, not accuracy.
